ledger.x: c. 314/3: Antigonus founds the League of the Islanders. 'In 314/3 BC, Antigonus I Monophthalmus sent a fleet under his nephew Dioscurides'; the League was founded 'c. 314/3 BC' under his auspices (a 306 date is often cited; Meadows argues Ptolemy II sponsored it). Antigonus's realm is inside macedonian-empire until…

c. 314/3: the League under Antigonus's auspices (his realm is macedonian-empire's until 306). Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord). It continued 'despite the defeat and death of Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BC'.
306: the patron's realm becomes the Antigonid kingdom.
306: the League as an Antigonid client.
c. 287/6: Antigonid protection ends when Seleucus I captures Demetrius.

c. 287/6: the Ptolemies take over. After Seleucus I captured Demetrius 'c. 287/6 BC' the islands passed to Ptolemaic hegemony; their games were renamed 'in honour of Ptolemy I Soter and his son Ptolemy II Philadelphus'.

c. 260: the first League fades and the Ptolemaic hegemony lapses. 'no nēsiarchos is attested after c. 260 BC' (verbatim). The League page: 'The islands remained under Ptolemaic control until sometime in the middle of the 3rd century BC' and 'the Ptolemaic position collapsed completely after Andros' (verbatim…

c. 260 to 201: the islands pass out of the League's hands and no state holds them on the pages. The League page says scholars disagree: 'suggested that the Ptolemaic withdrawal resulted in a Macedonian hegemony over the Cyclades' (verbatim fragment), Rhodes 'stepped into the power vacuum, concluding alliances with…

c. 200: the Second League under Rhodes takes the islands back from Philip V. The League was re-founded 'under the leadership of Rhodes in c. 200 BC' and 'survived until c. 167 BC'; 'In 201 BC, during the Cretan War, Philip V of Macedon subdued the Cyclades at the head of his fleet' (League page). The Cretan War page…
c. 200: Rhodes as hegemon. Rhodes was the hegemon of the Second League (League page, paraphrased).
167: the League of the Islanders ends.

wars.name: Cretan War
wars.outcome: Philip V subdued the Cyclades in 201 (League page); the Rhodians 'regained control over the Cyclades and reconfirmed their naval supremacy over the Aegean' (Cretan War page) and led the Second League from c.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Followed by further Macedonian setbacks in the Second Macedonian War (200-197 BC)'; no Cycladic border change is on the page.

certainty.note: The pages name member islands but no frontier; the Cyclades region is a stand-in, and the League was an association of island poleis.
